defs.def: one side or both sides of a sheet of paper in a book, magazine, etc. （书刊或纸张的）页，面，张，版

ex.s: Hardly had I written half a page when I felt a sharp pain in my chest
ex.t: 我刚写了半页，就感到胸口一阵剧痛

ex.s: With paper, there is a literal laying on of hands, along with the visual geography of distinct pages.
ex.t: 拿着纸书时，你能实实在在地用手翻阅，还能看到一页页分明的视觉布局。

ex.s: Of course, with its 2,672 pages, it's not exactly short.
ex.t: 当然，它有2672页，实在算不上“简编”。

ex.s: Campbell’s point is to wake up those responsible for AI—the technology companies and world leaders—so they are on the same page as all the experts currently developing it.
ex.t: 坎贝尔的目的是唤醒那些对人工智能负责的人——科技公司和世界领导人——让他们与目前开发人工智能的所有专家达成共识。

ex.s: Continued developments in communication technologies were once believed to make the printed page outdated.
ex.t: 通信技术的不断发展曾让人们以为印刷书页将会过时。

ex.s: To serve its function, a book must be activated by a user: the cover opened, the pages parted, the contents reviewed, perhaps notes written down or words underlined.
ex.t: 为了发挥其功能，一本书必须由使用者来激活：打开封面，翻开书页，浏览内容，也许还要写下笔记或划出字句。

ex.s: Then I turned the page and continued.
ex.t: 然后我翻过一页，继续读。

ex.s: Mr Titterton is chairman of the Omega Ensemble but has been the group’s official page turner for the past four years.
ex.t: 蒂特顿先生是Omega乐团的主席，但在过去四年里他一直是该乐团的官方翻谱员。

ex.s: His job is to sit beside the pianist and turn the pages of the score so the musicians don’t have to break the flow of sound by doing it themselves.
ex.t: 他的工作是坐在钢琴家旁边翻乐谱，这样音乐家就不必自己翻谱而打断音乐的流畅性。

ex.s: Being a page turner requires plenty of practice.
ex.t: 做一名翻谱员需要大量练习。

ex.s: “My husband is the worst page turner,” she laughed.
ex.t: "我丈夫是最糟糕的翻谱员，"她笑着说。

ex.s: “He’s interested in the music, feeling every note, and I have to say: ‘Turn, turn!’ “Robert is the best page turner I’ve had in my entire life.”
ex.t: "他对音乐很投入，感受每一个音符，而我不得不说：'翻页！翻页！'罗伯特是我一生中遇到过的最好的翻谱员。"

ex.s: What should Titterton be able to do to be a page turner?
ex.t: 蒂特顿要成为翻谱员需要能够做什么？

ex.s: Counting the pages.
ex.t: 数页数。

ex.s: Why is Ms Raspopova’s husband “the worse page turner”?
ex.t: 为什么拉斯波波娃女士的丈夫是"最糟糕的翻谱员"？

ex.s: In the latter you may only be able to read one page.
ex.t: 在后一种情况下，你可能只能读一页。

ex.s: It is enough to put the page number and one or two words as a reminder .
ex.t: 记下页码和一两个词作为提醒就足够了。

ex.s: Turn the page in your journal.
ex.t: 用文字表达你为什么感觉自己不值得，为什么你感觉不够好。

ex.s: 40   Turn to a page in your journal to your list of strengths and achievements.
ex.t: 40 　翻开日记本的一页，看你的优点和成就清单。

ex.s: At the top of a second page, put the heading “Acts of kindness.” On this one, list all the positive things you’ve done for others.
ex.t: 在第二页的顶部写下标题“善举”。在这一页上，列出你为他人做过的所有积极的事情。

ex.s: While going through the pages, he kept saying, wide-eyed: “How can there be this many words?” After a while, he looked at me and asked, “Do you know all these words, Mom?” I smiled, “I definitely do not know all these words,” I said.
ex.t: 他翻着书页，睁大眼睛不停地说：“怎么会有这么多词？”过了一会儿，他看着我问：“妈妈，你认识所有这些词吗？”我笑着说：“我确实不认识所有这些词。”

ex.s: Some pieces of music can go for 40 minutes and require up to 50 page turns, including back turns for repeat passages.
ex.t: 一些音乐片段可以进行40分钟，需要长达50页的翻转，包括重复段落的回转。

ex.s: More recently, as books have become inexpensive or even throwaway, artists have used them as the raw material for artworks — transforming covers, pages or even complete volumes into paintings and sculptures.
ex.t: 更近一些时候，随着书籍变得廉价甚至可以随意丢弃，艺术家们开始把它们用作艺术品的原材料——把封面、书页甚至整册书变成绘画和雕塑。

ex.s: “I was turning the page to get ready for the next page, but the draft wind from the turn caused the spare pages to fall off the stand,” Mr Titterton said, “Luckily I was able to catch them and put them back.”
ex.t: “我正翻页准备下一页，但翻页带起的气流把备用的谱子从谱架上吹掉了，”蒂特顿先生说，“幸好我接住了它们并放回去。”

ex.s: You have to make sure you don’t turn two pages at once and make sure you find the repeats in the music when you have to go back to the right spot.” Mr Titterton explained.
ex.t: 你必须确保一次不要翻两页，还要确保当你需要回到正确位置时能找到反复演奏的部分。"蒂特顿先生解释道。

ex.s: Silent onstage communication is key, and each pianist has their own style of “nodding” to indicate a page turn which they need to practise with their page turner.
ex.t: 台上无声的沟通是关键，每位钢琴家都有自己的点头风格来表示翻页，需要与翻谱员练习。

defs.def: a section of data or information that can be shown on a computer screen at any one time （计算机的）页面，版面

ex.s: People often link their memory of what they’ve read to how far into the book it was or where it was on the page.
ex.t: 人们常把对所读内容的记忆与它出现在书中的位置或页面上的位置联系起来。

ex.s: As I read, he reaches out and pokes（戳）the page with his finger.
ex.t: 当我读书时，他伸出手用手指戳（戳）页面。

ex.s: He poked the page even harder.
ex.t: 他更用力地戳了页面。

ex.s: Make a note of any page which is of special importance.
ex.t: 你可能会发现自己需要背诵某些内容。

ex.s: Triggering events for anger are so many that to describe them all would take hundreds of pages.
ex.t: 理解这些原因将控制我们自己的愤怒，如果我们愿意以批判的眼光评估自己。

ex.s: In his spare time though he goes on stage beside pianist Maria Raspopova — not as a musician but as her page turner.
ex.t: 但在空闲时间，他登上舞台，站在钢琴家玛丽亚·拉斯波波娃身旁——不是作为音乐家，而是作为她的翻谱员。

defs.def: an important event or period of history 历史篇章，历史篇页（指历史大事或时期）
a student who works as an assistant to a member of the US Congress （美国议员的）青年助理（本身为学生）

ex.s: The students took on diverse topics and turned in stories, 10 to 20 pages each, with characters that broadened my view and touched my heart.
ex.t: 学生们选择了各种不同的主题，交上来的故事每篇10到20页，其中的人物开阔了我的视野，也触动了我的心。

ex.s: Student A: Turn to Page 81.
ex.t: 学生A：翻到第81页。

ex.s: Student B: Turn to Page 84.
ex.t: 学生B：翻到第84页。

ex.s: Student A: Turn to Page 82.
ex.t: 学生A：翻到第82页。

ex.s: Student B: Turn to Page 85.
ex.t: 学生B：翻到第85页。

ex.s: Then, they will introduce their supporting arguments with expressions such as We must remember that… and We can’t deny that… Student A: Turn to Page 83.
ex.t: 然后，他们会用“我们必须记住……”和“我们不能否认……”这样的表达引出支撑论点。学生A：翻到第83页。

ex.s: Most page turners are piano students or up-and-coming concert pianists, although Ms Raspopova has once asked her husband to help her out on stage.
ex.t: 大多数翻谱员是钢琴学生或崭露头角的音乐会钢琴家，尽管拉斯波波娃女士曾经让她丈夫在台上帮忙。

ex.s: They could have written pages on the necessity of computers, but writing, in and of itself, simply didn’t strike them as important.
ex.t: 他冲出希尔家，快速穿过街道。

defs.def: a boy or young man who worked for a knight while training to be a knight himself 中世纪
to call sb's name over a public address system in order to find them and give them a message （在公共传呼系统上）呼叫
to contact sb by sending a message to their pager 用传呼机传呼（某人）

chunks.cn: 通常与 the 连用 页
